transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi. Um... I guess I'm here because... I just feel like I'm always running hot. Like I can't really shut the motor off. And, uh... lately that's been getting me in some trouble at the firehouse. So... that's why I'm here.
What kind of trouble have you been getting into at the firehouse?

Well... it's just... I guess I'm losing their trust a bit. We had to have a, uh, performance and safety meeting about me. They just... they feel like they can't count on me to keep track of the details. And, you know, I was hoping to move up, get into leadership, but... feels like that's slipping away now.
How long have you felt like your motor is always running?

Um... I don't know, it's been a real problem for... maybe a year and five months? Give or take. 

That's just... when things changed at work. We started doing these longer rotating shifts. And, uh... they added a bunch of extra documentation we have to do now. Plus some new drone duties. So... yeah. Since around then, I guess.
Did you ever have trouble with focus or feeling like a motor was running back when you were a child, before the age of twelve?

Um... yeah. I guess so. My mom, uh... she says I was like this back in grade school, too. 

She told me I was always getting out of my seat... blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking. I was always losing my homework, too. Got a lot of notes sent home. She always said I was bright enough to do the work, just... couldn't keep it together, I guess. So... yeah. Since I was a kid.
In your daily life recently, do you often find yourself interrupting others or finishing their sentences before they can?

Yeah, sometimes. At the station... when the guys are talking through a plan. 

I just... the answer is already in my head, you know? So I just cut in. I don't mean to. I just do it. And then... I realize I stepped on somebody's toes or messed up the flow of the discussion. So, yeah. I guess I do that.
